description: Verify that DUT discards an ICMP Echo Request whose IPv4 header carries malformed options (Internet Timestamp with length/pointer mismatch) and does NOT emit an Echo Reply — IP options are checked before ICMP is processed (RFC 791 §3.1 + RFC 792 Parameter Problem MUST)
approach:
[Objective]
The IP layer must reject malformed options before handing the payload up to ICMP. So even a structurally valid Echo Request that arrives wrapped in a header with bad options must be dropped — no Echo Reply.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: IPv4 + ICMP Echo Request
   • IP options = malformed Internet Timestamp (length=10 byte claims, only 8 B present; pointer past length+1)
   • ICMP body  = valid Echo Request
   • L2 dst     = DUT MAC (unicast)

2. Observation (5 s window):
   • DUT → Tester: no Echo Reply

[Pass condition]
DUT does not emit any Echo Reply within the window.

[Fail condition]
Fail_dut_replied — DUT replied to the Echo Request despite the malformed IP options. Indicates the IP layer passed the packet up before validating options.

verdicts.Pass: DUT dropped the Echo Request at the IP-options stage — normal
verdicts.Fail_dut_replied: DUT replied despite malformed IP options — option validation skipped
